lines.text: A single quarter of $321.4 million in adjusted EBITDA does not fix a broken balance sheet. lines.speaker: bull
lines.text: That $632.4 million net loss from 2025 is backward-looking and includes $313.4 million in non-cash depreciation and amortization. Meanwhile, S&P Global Ratings raised AMC's credit rating to B- from CCC+ in July 2026. The company also holds $428.5 million in cash and cash equivalents, giving it plenty of breathing room.

lines.speaker: bear
lines.text: Even excluding $313.4 million in depreciation and amortization, cash flow falls dangerously short. Interest coverage sits at a razor-thin 0.64x, meaning operational earnings cannot even cover annual interest expense of $459.5 million. Furthermore, floating-rate debt accounts for 49.9% of the total load, leaving lenders exposed to rising interest costs.

lines.text: Bear, you pointed out that floating-rate debt comprises 49.9% of total debt, but this claim was flagged as unsupported. How do you reconcile that figure given annual interest expense of $459.5 million against $4 billion in total debt?

lines.speaker: bear
lines.text: The 49.9% floating-rate debt figure directly stems from the nearly $2 billion term loan due 2029 carrying a floating 10.731% rate out of $4 billion in total debt. This heavy floating exposure is a primary driver behind the massive $459.5 million in annual interest expense. In fact, a simple 100-basis point rate increase adds approximately $20.1 million to annual interest expense on those term loans.
